items.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020
items.q: his solos with Ron Carter and Steve Coon and those guys, and Grady Tate, they were really great.

ctx.x: Yeah. You know what you said about your father being able to play and write equally well, it, I’m thinking of this record and I’ve been revisiting this. I still hold on to my favorite LPs. And there’s a quote from him in the liner notes. He said, “I get tired of all these guys having all the fun on my dates” so he gave himself some solos.

That’s right. And actually his solos with Ron Carter and Steve Coon and those guys, and Grady Tate, they were really great. He played well. But you know what I think helps and I’m learning that Hubert actually told me this, he said, “Dad played like a composer.” So he was always thinking. And that’s the thing — you know some of us get up and we just start blowing the little licks we’ve learned, but to really think about what you’re doing and Jamey Aebersold pushes that idea of really thinking about what you’re…
Well go listen — I mean I’m sure you’ve listened to this a few times. The original recording of “Stolen Moments” his tenor solo on there, he’s like, he’s composing as he goes, literally.
